title: Module 1 project: an order receipt
goal: Build a console program from an input contract to a checked order receipt.

prerequisites.text: Calculate integer quotient, remainder, and price.

terms.title: Program contract
terms.definition: A description of accepted input, exact output, and how the program reports invalid input.

terms.title: Cent
terms.definition: One hundredth of a currency unit. Prices and totals here are stored as whole cents.

terms.title: Test case
terms.definition: An input with an expected observable result recorded before running.

sections.title: Before writing any code
paragraphs: A warehouse counts full boxes but pays for every part. An order supplies three numbers: the quantity, the price of one part in cents, and the box capacity. It needs the full-box count, loose parts, and overall price.
Division and remainder describe the packaging. Multiplying quantity by unit price gives the price of every part, including loose ones.
In the example, read_numbers handles input and range validation. Read the bounds, then find where main starts computing the result.

sections.title: A compact report for the warehouse
paragraphs: The warehouse operator expects a compact report. For 5 parts at 80 cents with capacity 2, predict both packaging numbers and the total.
The example reads the first line, up to 79 bytes. Its three whitespace-separated values are quantity 0–500, unit price 0–1000, and capacity 1–100. Invalid input gives invalid.
steps: Quantity 5 and capacity 2 pass validation. 5 / 2 gives 2 boxes and 5 % 2 gives 1 loose part.
The total is 5 * 80 = 400 cents. Convert quantity to long before multiplying to accommodate totals up to 500000, even on an implementation with a 16-bit int.
The first printf combines packaging information, and the second prints the long total with %ld.
trace: Two full boxes and one loose part
The price of all five parts

sections.title: Cases that are easy to miss
paragraphs: Charging only for parts in full boxes would give 320 instead of 400 in the example. The price includes the loose part.
In long cents = quantity * unit_cost, the multiplication of ints is still performed first. Convert an operand before multiplying and print the resulting long with %ld.

sections.title: From a compact report to a receipt
paragraphs: The warehouse report uses two lines and the next screen expects three with exact labels. Check the calculations and the output format separately.
Write down expectations for normal, boundary, and invalid input. Reject zero capacity before calculating and accept an order containing zero parts.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check how the common arithmetic type is selected and how printf formats long.

feedback: That charges only the four parts in full boxes.

selfcheck.prompt: How do you ensure that the multiplication is performed with long operands?
options: quantity * unit_cost on the right side of long cents
feedback: The first operand already has type long.
Inside the parentheses the multiplication still takes place as int.
The type of the result variable cannot change a completed multiplication.

selfcheck.prompt: Why is an empty order allowed while zero capacity is invalid? Which inputs test this difference?
selfcheck.feedback: Zero quantity gives zero boxes, loose parts, and cents with positive capacity, as in 0 350 4. Zero capacity prevents division, so an input such as 7 125 0 gives invalid.

practice.title: Collection receipt
practice.task: Create a three-line order receipt. The first input line (up to 79 bytes) provides quantity 0–500, unit price 0–1000 cents, and capacity 1–100 separated by whitespace. Print boxes: and the number of full boxes, loose: and the remainder, then total: and the price of all items followed by cents. Print invalid for an invalid first line.

cases.label: Seven items in groups of three

criteria: Input 7 125 3 produces boxes: 2, loose: 1, and total: 875 cents on separate lines.
An empty order, free items, maximum values, and invalid input were tested.
The total uses the entire quantity and long arithmetic. An invalid case produces only invalid.
practice.hint: The example uses the input in three different calculations. The starter shows the receipt layout. Work out the expression that produces each number.

steps.action: Read the contract and predict the result for 7 125 3 before adding formulas.
steps.why: Each of the three output fields comes from a different calculation.
steps.expected: Record 2 boxes, 1 loose item, and 875 cents.

steps.action: Add the calculations and run cases with a remainder, with zeros, and at maximum values.
steps.why: The maximum shows why the total type and format matter.

steps.action: Test the input with an extra field and a new input of your own.
steps.why: Invalid input stops before the calculation.
steps.expected: The rejected input prints invalid and the additional test has an exact prediction.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Choose two valid inputs with the same quantity and price but different box capacities. Find two different packaging results and explain why the total remains the same.
criteria: For example 9 42 4 gives 2 boxes and 1 loose part, while 9 42 6 gives 1 box and 3 loose parts.
Explain the dependence on quantity and price.

teaching.scene: A warehouse needs to pack every part and charge for every part. Derive both packing and price in cents from one input line, then test them independently.

predict.prompt: The sample reads 5, 80 and 2. How many full bundles and loose parts appear on the first line? What price appears on the second?
predict.answer: At capacity 2, two bundles use four parts and one is loose. All five cost 5 × 80 = 400 cents. The two lines are 2 bundles, 1 loose and 400 cents.

apply.prompt: With quantity 8, price 45 and capacity 3, predict the two packing figures and the total. Which test separately checks the zero-capacity rule?
apply.answer: Two bundles use six parts, two remain loose and the cost is 360 cents. Repeat the input with capacity 0 and expect only invalid.

practice.strategy: Label the role of each input value first. Keep the early validation, compute packing and total separately, then place the labels boxes, loose and total in order.
practice.diagnosis: If the total for seven parts charges for only the six packed ones, inspect which quantity is multiplied. Any output for capacity 0 calls for checking the early rejection before division.

syntax.example:
int quantity = 8, capacity = 3, price = 45;
long cents = (long)quantity * price;
syntax.explanation: Accepted input supplies three values in order. Packing uses capacity, and multiplication prices every part. Conversion before `*` makes the product a long.
syntax.mistake: Multiplying by the number of boxes or packed parts gives another price. Use the original quantity.
